To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
AirSense is an innovative system that can monitor air quality at both micro and macro levels.
we have proposed a low-cost air quality monitoring system for city that uses smartphones and low-cost air quality sensors for sensing and cloud for processing.

(i) the AirSense prototype has been implemented and the prototype has been evaluated, (ii) the prototype can provide an air quality index (AQI) of a city based on the data collected from various AQMDs and smartphones, (iii) the prototype can also generate an aggregate view of the city's air quality and (iv) the prototype can generate a pollution footprint of a person for the whole day.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, implementation and evaluation of an opportunistic crowd sensing based air quality monitoring and analysis system.
developing an air quality monitoring system that is able to collect and analyze data from a large number of sensors and smartphones to provide an aggregate view for the city.

the design and implementation of a low power and low-cost air quality sensing device and a crowd-sensing based framework that can be used to collect and aggregate data to monitor air quality at micro and macro level.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Airsense is a low cost, light weight and low power air quality monitoring system that provides a holistic view of air pollution in the city.
the system is a step towards a smart city.
AirSense is an effective, scalable, and low cost system that can provide air quality information to citizens and authorities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AirSense provides an end-to-end system for sensing and monitoring air quality in the vicinity and the city.

we have developed an opportunistic crowd sensing based air quality monitoring platform that is able to collect and aggregate sensor data from multiple users and multiple devices to provide an air quality index map for the city and also provide an individual pollution footprint for the end user.
AirSense can be used for monitoring air quality in the city and it can also be used to monitor air quality in the vicinity of a building or a neighborhood.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the proposed opportunistic crowd-sensed air pollution monitoring system can provide an aggregate view of the air pollution of the city, and can help citizens to make informed decisions about air quality.
the crowd can collaboratively sense air quality in the city and provide an aggregate view for the city and its citizens to take informed decisions.
opportunistic crowd-sensed data can be effectively used in smart cities to provide an aggregated view of air quality of the city and its neighbourhood.
